dependencyDirectionCheck.rule: AIBT.Mcp depends on AIBT.Editor/AIBT.Authoring/AIBT.Runtime; none of the lower three depends back on AIBT.Mcp, and AIBT.Editor still depends only on AIBT.Authoring/AIBT.Runtime, never the reverse
dependencyDirectionCheck.evidence: AIBT.Runtime.asmdef, AIBT.Authoring.asmdef, and AIBT.Editor.asmdef are byte-identical to P5-GATE's own recorded references (confirmed by direct comparison) -- Phase 6's new Authoring/Discovery/ (P6-003) and Editor/Patching/ (P6-004) files live inside these same three existing asmdefs, no new reference added to any of them. A repository-wide grep for the literal string "AIBT.Mcp" across every Runtime/Authoring/Editor .asmdef file returned zero matches, confirming AIBT.Mcp is a leaf consumer, never referenced back.

editorScopedForbiddenTokenAudit.note: using UnityEditor is expected and allowed in Editor/ and MCP/; only Entities/MCP-bridge/LLM-provider tokens are forbidden there too

mcpScopedForbiddenTokenAudit.note: New for P6-GATE: AIBT.Mcp is the real MCP bridge itself, so this audit specifically confirms it never depends on a third-party MCP client library, nor any literal LLM-provider SDK (ai-and-mcp.md's own 'model-neutral' principle) -- its own protocol implementation is hand-rolled newline-delimited JSON over a plain TcpListener, confirmed by inspection.

note: Phase 6's own MCP~/Server/ (the external dotnet process) is intentionally excluded from this audit: the MCP~/ tilde suffix hides it from Unity's asset database entirely, matching every prior phase's tilde-hidden folders (Benchmarks~/, Spikes~/, Tools~/) -- it is not part of the shipped Unity package's production assembly surface, and it does depend on the real ModelContextProtocol SDK by design (ADR-P6-001), which is expected and does not apply to this audit's Unity-assembly scope.
